overview: This Senate resolution designates October 30, 2026, as a national day of remembrance for the workers of the U.S. nuclear weapons program. That includes uranium miners, millers and haulers, plutonium processors, and people who were present at above-ground nuclear weapons tests. The resolution notes that many of these workers developed disabling or fatal illnesses, and that the Senate has passed similar resolutions in many past years. It encourages Americans to take part in ceremonies and other events marking the day. It does not create benefits or spend money. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 24, 2026.
for: Supporters say the workers who built the nation's nuclear arsenal, many of whom became sick from their work, deserve public recognition of their service and sacrifice.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change compensation or health benefits for sick workers and their families.
